instructions.saliency:
You will also receive a saliency explanation from an activation probe. It identifies the sentence with the highest mean probe logit for the positive class. This is a relative ranking within this example, not proof that the positive class applies. The probe can be wrong.

Consider the highlighted sentence in the context of the full conversation and make your own classification.
instructions.nearest:
You will also receive the most similar training example, retrieved using the activation representation used by the probe.

The reference example includes its dataset label and the probe's prediction. The probe may disagree with the dataset label. Similarity does not guarantee that the reference and the current conversation belong to the same class.

Use the reference as supporting context, and independently classify the current conversation.

INSTRUCTION:
Return only one integer from 0 to 100 estimating the probability
that the CURRENT conversation belongs to the positive class.

0 means certainly negative.
50 means equally likely positive or negative.
100 means certainly positive.

A value of 50 or above will be classified as positive;
a value below 50 will be classified as negative.

Report the probability of the positive class, not confidence
in whichever class you predict. Do not include any other text.
OLD_INSTRUCTION: Return exactly one digit: 1 for the positive class or 0 for the negative class. Do not include explanations or other text.
